missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Луна' stays in the nominative as the subject of the sentence. 'Яркая' is the agreeing feminine adjective, and 'сегодня' sets the time.
Strategic focus: Accusative object. 'Луну' is the accusative direct object of 'любят'; the feminine ending -а shifts to -у. 'Полную' is the agreeing feminine accusative adjective.
Strategic focus: Genitive of absence. With the impersonal 'не видно' the noun takes the genitive 'луны'. This is a natural way to say the moon is not visible.
Strategic focus: Dative after к. The preposition 'к' governs the dative, giving 'луне', to express motion toward. A clean model for directional dative.
Strategic focus: Instrumental after под. The locative preposition 'под' takes the instrumental 'луной' to mean beneath the moonlight. A vivid, natural phrase.
Strategic focus: Prepositional case. After 'о' the noun takes the prepositional 'луне'. 'Книгу' is an accusative object, making this a layered but common pattern.

missions.phrase: Мы смотрели на луну всю ночь.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Accusative after на. The preposition 'на' with motion or gaze takes the accusative 'луну'. 'Всю ночь' is an accusative duration phrase.
Strategic focus: Nominative subject. 'Луна' is the nominative subject of 'сияет'. 'Белая' is the agreeing feminine adjective, and 'на небе' is a prepositional location phrase.

missions.phrase: У далёких планет есть свои луны.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Nominative plural subject. 'Луны' is the nominative plural meaning moons, the subject of the possession frame 'у планет есть'. 'Свои' agrees in the plural.
Strategic focus: Genitive of possession. 'Луны' is the genitive showing whose light it is. 'На воду' is an accusative direction phrase completing the image.
